name: Bidens

project_scope.admission_note: Both source-pool species approved for learner; native-range UNRESOLVED until target-county audit.
project_scope.range_note: Both UNRESOLVED, no automatic native PASS; additional comparison-only taxa not installed.

shared_genus_characters.look_here_first: Start with ONE leaf attached to a MIDDLE stem node: compound 3(–5) leaflets versus SIMPLE sessile blade. Then look at the actual OUTER green calyculus (extra bract ring) and INNER phyllaries behind each disk/head. Finally magnify the ripe wedge-shaped CY­PSELA (fruit) and individual barbed AWNS; rays yellow/absent alone insufficient.
shared_genus_characters.shared: Opposite leaves often, Asteraceae heads with yellow/orange disk florets and optional rays. Two nested sets of bracts: outer green leaflike CALYCULUS bractlets, inner overlapping involucre PHYL­LARIES. Flattened fruit (cypsela, often wrongly called a seed) with 2–4 spine-like pappus AWNS whose barbs catch fur and clothing; awn count and anatomy vary across species.

glossary.plain: One whole leaf made of several individual small leaflets attached to one shared stalk.
One continuous blade on one leaf base, even when the margin is toothed.
Outer crown of often green, leaflike bractlets UNDER the main overlapping flower-head bracts.
One of the inner overlapping bracts wrapping around the disk/florets.
One strap-shaped individual flower, NOT one petal belonging to a larger flower.
The dry one-seeded FRUIT, like the sticky black beggartick 'seed'.
Pointed tip on cypsela bearing tiny hooks; often two or more like a tiny pitchfork.
Barbs point BACK toward the base/fruit, like a fishhook.
Barbs point FORWARD toward the awn tip; some frondosa awns and fruit margins vary.

species_comparison_matrix.leaf: Opposite petiolate compound leaves usually 3, sometimes 5 serrated leaflets
species_comparison_matrix.head: Ray florets 0 or 1–3, small (2–3.5 mm), inconspicuous; orange-yellow disk
species_comparison_matrix.bracts: Calyculus usually 5–8(–10), ciliolate outer green bractlets
species_comparison_matrix.fruit: Outer cypsela 5–7 mm, inner 7–10 mm; usually 2 barbed pappus awns ~2–5 mm
species_comparison_matrix.first: Find shared petiole for three leaflets attached to one stem leaf node
species_comparison_matrix.lookalike: B. vulgata (comparison-only) has compound or laciniate leaves too, but calyculus usually 10–16(–21) and more deeply cut leaflets.

species_comparison_matrix.growth: ANNUAL, sometimes persists (corrected 2026-10-12; NOT default perennial)
species_comparison_matrix.leaf: Opposite, usually sessile SIMPLE lanceolate/elliptic blades, coarse teeth often
species_comparison_matrix.head: Usually 7–8 yellow rays ~15–25 mm; occasionally rays absent
species_comparison_matrix.bracts: Calyculus often 5–7(–9+) bractlets, often spread/reflex; inner phyllaries ~8–12
species_comparison_matrix.fruit: Outer cypsela 6–8 mm, inner 8–10 mm; usually 2–4 awns ~3–5 mm; margins not conspicuously corky-winged
species_comparison_matrix.first: Find one entire simple leaf STILL attached at opposite stem node
species_comparison_matrix.lookalike: B. cernua (comparison-only) may have simple leaves & 6–8 rays, but rays often 2–15 mm; cypsela margins often thickened/winged and awns 1–4 mm. These overlap.

decision_sequence: 1. Take photo of middle STEM NODE with both opposite leaves and at least one full leaf attached. Count leaflets per LEAF, not leaves per NODE.
2. THREE separate toothed leaflets on common petiole? Favor B. frondosa, but check B. vulgata and calyculus bract number.
3. ONE long toothed SIMPLE sessile blade per leaf? Favor B. laevis, but B. cernua also simple; photograph flower head and mature fruits.
4. Turn intact HEAD SIDEWAYS: the extra longer green outer calyculus bractlets are outside/BELOW the inner shorter overlapping phyllaries; avoid counting inner as outer.
5. With 10× lens and millimeter scale, image a ripe dark CY­PSELA: how many barbed AWNS, do margins have conspicuous corky WINGS, and how long is fruit body vs awn?
6. If no mature fruit or reliable complete calyculus, identify Bidens sp. or cf. B. laevis/frondosa, rather than invent certainty.

head_to_head.first: At MIDDLE stem node, frondosa = ONE compound leaf divided into typically THREE leaflet blades on a shared stalk. Laevis = ONE undivided serrate blade per leaf, sessile/opposite. Frondosa flower head mainly disks, laevis often showy 7–8 rays. Check actual head/fruit anatomy and not color alone.
head_to_head.photo: Paired WHOLE leaves with node/base visible, then both heads with outer calyculus bractlets and inner phyllaries.

head_to_head.pair: Bidens frondosa vs Bidens vulgata (comparison only)
head_to_head.first: BOTH can be compound-leaved with tiny/absent ray florets; count OUTER calyculus bractlets around the mature head: frondosa ~5–8(–10), vulgata ~10–16(–21). Vulgata often has more deeply laciniate/lobed leaves; variable, don't force ID when count overlaps.
head_to_head.photo: Face view showing entire branching compound leaf, head SIDE 360-degree calyculus count; ripe barbed cypselae.

head_to_head.pair: Bidens laevis vs Bidens cernua (comparison only)
head_to_head.first: Both SIMPLE sessile leaves and yellow rays in wetlands. Laevis often longer rays ~15–25 mm and fruit margins not notably winged; cernua rays commonly 2–15 mm and mature cypsela margins thickened or corky-winged, usually shorter awns. Nodding in fruit occurs in BOTH.
head_to_head.photo: Matched measured rays and OUTER CY­PSELA edge at ≥10× with 1mm ruler; head profile with green outer calyculus visible.

visual_comparison.title: Beggarticks — see the leaf FIRST, then green bracts and sticky fruits
visual_comparison.subtitle: Two canonical species, five real source-attributed photographs covering habit, whole leaf, head, and fruits. All are real source/physical images; no unverified arrows.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: FRO(N)DOSA: leaf FRACTIONS (3–5) + mostly disk head; LAEVIS: ONE leaf blade + often large yellow rays. For look-alikes, count OUTER calyculus bracts and examine ripe fruit margins.
